evidence: Plin. NH 16.162: harundinī Indicae arborea amplitūdō (Lewis & Short s.v. arboreus)
terms.comment: Pliny’s Indian reed, which grows to the size of a tree: the bamboo, as Morgan–Owens identifies it and Levi and Bini give it. For a cane or a stick of it, plain harundō serves (see “reed”).

phrases.latin: Harundō Indica celerrimē crēscit: paucīs mēnsibus tēctum superat.
phrases.english: Bamboo grows very fast: in a few months it’s taller than the roof.
We’ll build a hut out of bamboo.

sources: Lewis & Short: harundo · Lewis & Short: arboreus
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. bamboo.
Enrico Levi and Arturo Bini, Il latino come lingua viva (1937), p. 9, s.v. bambù.
